Lemma
[Metric-Preserving Maps Do Not Increase Distance]

↗ def:metric-preserving ↗ def:riemannian-distance ↗ prop:length-isometry-invariant

If $\varphi :(M,g)\to (\widetilde M,\widetilde g)$ is smooth and metric-preserving, then \[ d_{\widetilde g}(\varphi (x),\varphi (y))\le d_g(x,y), \qquad x,y\in M. \]
Proof

↗ prop:length-isometry-invariant ↗ def:riemannian-distance \sketch For $r>d_g(x,y)$ choose a competitor $\gamma $ of length below $r$. Proposition 14 gives the same length for $\varphi \circ \gamma $, so $d_{\widetilde g}(\varphi (x),\varphi (y))<r$. Let $r$ decrease to $d_g(x,y)$.

□

The inequality can be strict because the target may contain shorter curves outside the image.
